title: 일이 꼬였을 때 이유 말하기: 탓에·바람에·통에
objective: By the end, you can form -는 탓에, -(으)ㄴ 탓에, -는 바람에, and -는 통에 correctly. You can also choose the one that fits the cause: a fault or bad habit, a sudden event, or a noisy, busy situation.
summary: Learn three ways to give the cause of a bad result in Korean: -는 탓에, -는 바람에, and -는 통에.

task.title: Explain what went wrong
task.line: Follow the English instruction in each item and write or choose the correct Korean form.

forms.when: With verbs, for a situation or habit that is still going on. Use N 탓에 after nouns.
forms.means: Because of (and it's that cause's fault). Shows blame or regret for a bad result.
forms.example: 요즘 밤늦게까지 휴대폰을 보는 탓에 아침마다 피곤해요.
forms.exampleMeaning: I'm tired every morning these days because I look at my phone until late at night.

forms.when: With verbs for something that already happened. With adjectives for a state.
forms.means: Because (something) happened, or because (something) is a certain way. The result is bad.
forms.example: 어제 늦게 잔 탓에 수업 시간에 졸았어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: I dozed off in class because I went to bed late last night.

forms.when: With verbs only, and always the -는 form, even for past events. Put the tense at the end of the sentence.
forms.means: Because something sudden or unexpected happened, I couldn't avoid a bad result.
forms.example: 휴대폰이 갑자기 꺼지는 바람에 친구에게 연락을 못 했어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: My phone suddenly turned off, so I couldn't contact my friend.

forms.when: With verbs, for a noisy, busy, or chaotic situation (people talking loudly, construction, moving house).
forms.means: Because of all the noise or commotion, something went badly.
forms.example: 옆집에서 공사하는 통에 주말에 제대로 못 쉬었어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: I couldn't rest properly on the weekend because of the construction next door.

watchOut: 비가 왔는 바람에 (X) → 비가 오는 바람에 (O): -는 바람에 never changes. Show the past at the end: 비가 오는 바람에 늦었어요.
방이 좁은 바람에 (X) → 방이 좁은 탓에 (O): 바람에 and 통에 go with verbs. Use -(으)ㄴ 탓에 with adjectives.
택시를 타는 바람에 일찍 도착했어요 (X) → 택시를 탄 덕분에 일찍 도착했어요 (O): These three are for bad results. For good results, use 덕분에.
차가 막히는 바람에 일찍 출발하세요 (X) → 차가 막히니까 일찍 출발하세요 (O): Don't end these sentences with a command or suggestion. Use -(으)니까 instead.
exercises: Fill in the blank with the -는 바람에 form of 오다: 출근길에 갑자기 소나기가 ____ 옷이 다 젖었어요.
Fill in the blank with the -는 통에 form of 떠들다: 룸메이트 친구들이 밤마다 ____ 시험공부를 제대로 못 했어요.
Fill in the blank with the 탓에 form of 비싸다: 이 동네는 집값이 ____ 젊은 사람들이 많이 떠나요.

Write O if the sentence is correct and X if it is wrong. If it is wrong, correct the expression that gives the reason (the part ending in 바람에 or 탓에): ① 날씨가 더운 바람에 입맛이 없어요. ② 지하철이 갑자기 멈추는 바람에 면접에 늦었어요. ③ 친구가 공항까지 태워 준 탓에 비행기를 놓치지 않았어요.
Join the two sentences into one with -는 바람에: 회의가 늦게 끝났어요. 마지막 기차를 놓쳤어요.
Answer the question in Korean with 탓에 and 운동을 안 하다: 요즘 왜 체력이 약해졌어요?
answers: ① X → 더운 탓에 ② O ③ X → 태워 준 덕분에
회의가 늦게 끝나는 바람에 마지막 기차를 놓쳤어요.
운동을 안 하는 탓에 체력이 약해졌어요. (운동을 안 한 탓에 체력이 약해졌어요.)
